source.title: On the Lipschitz Constant of Deep Networks and Double Descent
source.authors: Matteo Gamba; Hossein Azizpour; Mårten Björkman

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present, including appendices. No apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: It varies network width and measures test error, reporting double descent and a post-interpolation decline across several model families and datasets. This directly tests the width–test-error pattern in a different set of architectures and settings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports width sweeps and test-error trends relevant to V2. Its label-noise settings are not a test of fitting fully random labels; cited findings are not extracted as rows. Lipschitz and curvature results do not test V7's magnitude-aware weight-perturbation measure.
record.test_reason: The study measures training and held-out error across width sweeps in new architecture and task settings. Figure 1 explicitly reports post-interpolation test-error descent, bearing on V2.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate. The authors report empirical Lipschitz trends correlated with double descent and develop theoretical connections to loss-landscape geometry. They identify curvature and distance from initialization as factors associated with optimization dynamics and bounded function complexity, without establishing a complete causal explanation of generalization.
record.recipe_differences: Uses width sweeps and test error, but studies ConvNets, ResNet18s, and Transformers on CIFAR and translation tasks rather than the specified one-hidden-layer ReLU networks and datasets.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported test-error curves vary with architecture, dataset, label-noise setting, and model width; the paper does not give separate textual comparisons of the curve shapes by condition.

fits_no_version.finding: Empirical input-space Lipschitz constants, spectral-norm upper bounds, Hessian curvature, gradient-noise covariance, and distance from initialization broadly track model-wise double descent.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input sensitivity and several optimization-related complexity measures correlate with held-out error across model widths in the tested settings.

record.problems: Condition-specific curve values and uncertainty estimates are not stated in the text; plotted results are figure-only. The paper does not test random-label memorization.
record.rows_left_out: No additional version-mapped rows were omitted. The paper reports many other measurements (empirical Lipschitz constant, loss Jacobian norm, Hessian curvature, gradient-noise covariance, and distance from initialization); these do not measure the behaviors named in the listed versions, especially V7's magnitude-aware perturbation measure.

untested.parts: Perfect fitting of fully random labels, natural-label generalization under the same recipe, and chance-level held-out performance after random-label training.

The original one-hidden-layer ReLU setting on MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10; convergence-controlled comparisons beyond the reported finite training budgets. Translation experiments do not establish the zero-training-error prerequisite.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus nonadaptive optimizers and tuning-dependent differences.
Held-out performance under different batch sizes and training-budget adaptations.
The effect of adding or removing dropout.
Magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation tolerance, generalization-gap rankings, and comparisons against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V2. The interpolation peak itself is not a challenge to V2, which concerns widening beyond the fitting threshold. Numerical curve values are unavailable in the supplied text. Appendix B reports three ConvNet seeds and five ResNet seeds, although explicit uncertainty estimates are not provided.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report fitting fixed random labels and comparing their held-out accuracy with natural-label training.
Uses ConvNets, ResNet18s, and Transformers rather than one-hidden-layer ReLU networks; datasets and training details differ from the specified setting.
Does not compare convolutional networks with fully connected networks.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD.
Does not vary batch size or compare large- and small-batch training.
Measures empirical input-space Lipschitz constants and parameter-space curvature, not magnitude-aware weight perturbations or their ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Does not remove and retrain on selected training examples.

source_check.notes: Support is under finite training budgets, without a convergence-controlled comparison; exact condition-specific test errors remain figure-only. The supplied text is arXiv v5 dated July 2025 and identifies itself as the uncompressed BMVC 2023 final paper.

statements.correction: Appendix B: 3 random seeds for ConvNets; 5 for ResNets; seeds vary initialization and mini-batch sampling/shuffling. ConvNets: 500 epochs. ResNet18s: 4000 epochs. SGD with momentum; no explicit regularization. Section 3, CIFAR-10 with 20% corrupted labels: interpolation widths 14 for ConvNets and 5 for ResNets. Figure 1: test-error double descent for ConvNets, ResNets and Vision Transformers.
statements.problem: The width-sweep findings are supported, but the blanket assertion that this study lacks uncertainty checks overlooks its repeated-seed experiments. Explicit uncertainty intervals are not established by the supplied text.
